title: RationalTensorComparisonSystem
statement: For an integral system [def-sf-integral-tensor-comparison-system], use the raw scalar localizations of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]: objects are unchanged and Hom modules are localized, with no idempotent completion. A rational tensor comparison system records symmetric monoidal structures with tensor on objects inherited from the integral tensor and on pure arrows $(a\otimes f)\otimes(b\otimes g)=ab\otimes(f\otimes g)$, and constraints obtained by $1\otimes(-)$. It records perfect-valued functors with finite-dimensional bounded cohomology, object formula $F_E^{\mathrm{rat}}X=B_{E/R_E}F_EX$, arrow formula $F_E^{\mathrm{rat}}(a\otimes f)=a B_{E/R_E}(F_Ef)$, and tensor and unit comparisons $B(\tau)$ followed by the normalized balanced comparisons. It records the rationalized transitions, their tensorators, units, identities and tower maps, natural scalar comparisons $\phi$ and all their identity, tower, signed symmetry, tensor and unit equations. The comparison between derived $B$ and termwise field scalar extension is normalized on every complex by the canonical derived counit [lem-weil-derived-field-scalar-extension-tower]. The validity predicate requires the integral-to-rational scalar square for $\phi$, not an arbitrary comparison. This record asserts no existence.
